rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you so much for reaching out! I really appreciate the offer to help. I've crystallized what Halcyon Threshold is going to focus on: identifying neglected gaps in AI safety evaluation and building practical tools to fill those gaps. The core idea is that everyone's measuring what they're already measuring, but we don't have good processes for discovering what we're NOT measuring but should be. Your data analyst skills would be incredibly valuable for this. Here's what I'm thinking for concrete ways you could contribute (5 hrs/week): **Short term (next 2-4 weeks):** - Help me survey and categorize existing AI safety evaluation frameworks - Build a database/spreadsheet of what capabilities and risks are currently being measured by different orgs - Look for patterns in what's missing or underexplored **Medium term (next 3 months):** - Help analyze interview data as I talk to researchers about evaluation needs - Design data collection methodologies for the eval tools we build - Review and validate our gap analysis Does this sound interesting to you? No pressure if it's not the right fit, but if it is, I'd love to have you involved. I'm putting together a grant application for this (deadline Nov 30) and planning to start preliminary research immediately. The repo is at github.com/halcyonthreshold (I can add you as a collaborator). What do you think? Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Responded to Priya Raman with concrete project scope (5 hrs/week data analyst help)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Rapid grants application: AI Safety Evaluation Gap Analysis". It read: "Hi Idris, Thank you for encouraging me to apply! Attached is my two-page proposal for Halcyon Threshold's first project: systematically identifying neglected gaps in AI safety evaluation and building practical tools to fill them. **Quick summary:** - **What**: Survey existing eval frameworks, identify what's not being measured, build open-source tools for the highest-priority gaps - **Why me**: Technical skills (Python, data analysis), realistic scope for evenings/weekends, focus on infrastructure not novel research - **Budget**: $18,000 over 6 months - **Deliverables**: Published gap analysis, 3-5 open-source evaluation tools, case studies of adoption **Core insight**: Everyone measures what they're already measuring. We need systematic processes for discovering blind spots in AI safety evaluation before capabilities in those areas become dangerous. The full proposal is below. Happy to discuss or provide any additional information you need. Best, Morgan --- # Emberfall Fund Grant Proposal **Halcyon Threshold: AI Safety Evaluation Gap Analysis & Tools** Applicant: Morgan Hale (morgan@halcyonthreshold.org) Amount Requested: $18,000 Duration: 6 months (January - June 2027) Date: November 19, 2026 --- ## Project Summary We will systematically identify neglected areas in AI safety evaluation, then build practical open-source tools that enable other researchers to measure what's currently not being measured. ## The Problem Current AI safety evaluation efforts focus on known risks and capabilities. Major labs have sophisticated eval suites for things like power-seeking, deception, and dangerous capabilities. But there's a systematic blind spot: **we don't have good processes for discovering what we're NOT evaluating but should be**. As systems become more capable, the most important risks may be capabilities we haven't thought to test for. We need infrastructure for finding and filling these gaps. ## What We'll Do ### Phase 1: Comprehensive Gap Analysis (Months 1-2) - Survey all major AI safety evaluation frameworks (METR, DeepMind, Anthropic, Apollo Research, etc.) - Interview 15-20 safety researchers about evaluation needs - Map the landscape: what's being measured, what's not, and why - Create prioritized list of evaluation gaps by importance × neglectedness × tractability - Publish findings as open research ### Phase 2: Tool & Framework Development (Months 3-5) - Build 3-5 practical evaluation tools for highest-priority gaps - Create detailed methodologies and documentation - Release everything open-source (MIT license) - Focus on tools that: - Other researchers can actually use - Don't require massive compute or access - Address genuinely neglected capabilities/risks ### Phase 3: Validation & Iteration (Month 6) - Work with 3-5 research groups to pilot the tools - Gather feedback and iterate - Document case studies and learnings - Plan for sustainability (potential small-grants program in year 2) ## Deliverables 1. **Published research report**: \"AI Safety Evaluation Gaps: A Systematic Analysis\" (Month 2) 2. **Open-source evaluation toolkit**: 3-5 working tools with documentation (Month 5) 3. **Case studies**: Documentation of tools being used by other researchers (Month 6) 4. **All work in public repository**: Transparent, reproducible, forkable ## Why Me **Relevant background:** - Technical background: Python, data analysis, software development - Currently work in logistics operations (Dorrance Logistics), experience with risk assessment and process evaluation - Attending AI safety meetups and building connections in the community - Not claiming to be an AI safety expert - this is infrastructure work, not novel technical research **Why this project fits:** - I can contribute 15-20 hours per week (evenings/weekends) - I have a data analyst (Priya Raman) volunteering 5 hours/week to assist - This is tractable for a small team: we're not doing novel research, we're building infrastructure - My comparative advantage: being a skilled generalist who can talk to researchers and build tools **Accountability:** - All work will be in public GitHub repository - Monthly progress reports to Emberfall - Clear success metrics: tools must be adopted by others to count as successful ## Budget **Total: $18,000 over 6 months** | Item | Amount | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | Research time (Phase 1) | $4,000 | 80 hours @ $50/hr for interviews, analysis, writeup | | Development time (Phase 2) | $8,000 | 160 hours @ $50/hr for tool building, testing, documentation | | Validation & iteration (Phase 3) | $2,000 | 40 hours @ $50/hr working with pilot users | | Compute & infrastructure | $1,500 | Cloud compute for running test evals, hosting tools | | Research access & tools | $1,000 | API access, datasets, software licenses as needed | | Travel for interviews | $1,500 | 2-3 trips to meet with researchers in-person | **Notes on rate:** $50/hr is below my regular salary but reflects that this is part-time, mission-driven work. The grant enables me to dedicate serious time to this rather than fitting it around other freelance work. **Other funding:** I am contributing $2,000 of personal funds to cover preliminary research and setup costs through December 2026. ## Success Metrics **6-month metrics:** - Gap analysis published and cited by at least 2 other organizations - 3-5 evaluation tools completed and documented - At least 3 external research groups actively using the tools - Clear evidence we're enabling measurement of something genuinely neglected **12-month vision (beyond this grant):** - Tools in regular use across multiple organizations - Other researchers forking and extending our work - Potential for small-grants program to fund others to run evaluations we've designed ## Why Fund This **High neglectedness:** No one is systematically working on evaluation gap analysis as dedicated infrastructure. **High leverage:** Good tools enable many others to do important work. If even one of our tools catches …"
